clue.text: No address; more often away

definitions.meaning: having nowhere to live, so no fixed address
read as '...': at ... often, so out more

explanation.surface: Someone with no fixed abode is out and about more than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: someone who is at home less is more often away.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sleeping rough has no dwelling and therefore no postal address.

clue.text: New Year present for Humperdinck's hero, say.?

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to pronounce the hero's name, which matches the gift's name in speech

parts.note: Hansel is the boy in Humperdinck's opera Hansel and Gretel

explanation.surface: A seasonal gift chosen for the boy in Humperdinck's fairy-tale opera.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a handsel is a gift given at the start of the year, a token of good luck.

clue.text: Only one tool for this flying machine

parts.note: mono- is the prefix meaning single or only one
a plane is a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: A single implement is all that is needed for this aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tool' is the woodworker's plane, which also happens to be the flying sense of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft with a single pair of wings is the kind of flying machine described.

clue.text: Side-issue when Ballater's short of capital

indicators.note: what issues from the shortened town name is its letters brought out in a fresh order
lacking its capital letter, so the initial B of the town name goes

parts.note: Ballater is a town on Royal Deeside in Scotland

explanation.surface: A secondary matter arises when a Scottish town runs out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of capital' removes the capital B, leaving ALLATER; 'issue' then rearranges those letters. 'capital' looks like money but is the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means to the side, as in lateral movement or a lateral branch.

clue.text: The Sea Foam tie-up is more than enough

parts.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells us to read the word tie from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A merger involving a company called The Sea Foam is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie-up' looks like a merger; in the down light 'up' turns TIE to EIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an amount beyond what is needed.

clue.text: .Man of title loses heart to London borough.

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: a baronet holds a hereditary title, Sir before his name

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman gives up his affections to a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: BARONET has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnet is one of the boroughs of Greater London, on its northern edge.

clue.text: Polished off like Cleopatra's barge

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Enobarbus says 'The barge she sat in, like a burnish'd throne, burn'd on the water'

explanation.surface: Finished off in the style of the Egyptian queen's famous vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is a link here, making 'Polished off' look like 'finished'. The second definition is a quotation from Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal rubbed until it gleams is said to be burnished, and Shakespeare uses that word for the queen's gilded barge.

clue.text: Be waspish again when not acting

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sting is what a wasp does

explanation.surface: Someone is spiteful once more while out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waspish' suggests a sharp temper, but here it means doing what a wasp does. An actor between jobs is politely said to be resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical slang calls an unemployed actor resting, between engagements.

clue.text: Next, remember to be immoderate in this!

indicators.note: 'in this' points at the clue words just given, whose letters hold the answer

explanation.surface: A reminder that the following act should be excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'nEXT, REMEmber', ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extreme goes far beyond the reasonable, so it lacks moderation.

clue.text: He doesn't come under. orders

parts.note: a racehorse is 'under orders' at the start; one that fails to leave the stalls never runs

explanation.surface: A man who disobeys instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under orders' is the racing term for horses lined up for the start; the stray full stop after 'under' is a print speck.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that never starts a race is the original sense; the word now also means a plan with no chance.

clue.text: Here sound's O.K. for vision

indicators.note: the sound is right for the word vision, so the answer is said the same way

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: This venue has good acoustics and good sight lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place, the spot one indicates by saying 'here'.

clue.text: One of the film crowd, responsive but extremely touchy

parts.note: a super, short for supernumerary, is an extra in a crowd scene
sensitive means quick to respond

explanation.surface: A film extra who is receptive yet thin-skinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersensitive means abnormally easily hurt or offended.

clue.text: Sheet allowed to be handed round

parts.note: a leaf is a sheet of paper in a book
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A piece of paper permitted to be passed among the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' looks like the definition, but it is the first piece; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handout is distributed to people, passed from hand to hand.

clue.text: Recite tax-amendment to get out of a fix

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters of the two words are altered

explanation.surface: Reading out a change to the tax rules as a way to escape trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax-amendment' looks like a budget change, but 'amendment' rearranges RECITE and TAX together.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate means to free from a difficulty or entanglement.

clue.text: Strangling Eastern superstition

parts.note: the ritual murder by strangling practised by a religious cult of robbers in India

explanation.definitionFit: Thuggee was the practice of the Indian thugs, who strangled travellers as an offering to Kali.

clue.text: English is translated by a Teutonic expert

parts.note: Teutonic means of the Germanic peoples
the English word 'is' rendered in the other language becomes ist

explanation.surface: An English word put into German by a scholar of that tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a' is the link. The suffix -ist marks a specialist, so a Germanist is an expert in German language or culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Germanist is a scholar who specialises in German studies.

clue.text: What a witty soul!

parts.note: Polonius says that this quality is the soul of wit, so it is wit's soul

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a clever companion.
explanation.walkthrough: From Hamlet: 'brevity is the soul of wit'. The clue reads 'soul' as a person, but it is wit's essence.
explanation.definitionFit: Brevity means conciseness, which Shakespeare's Polonius calls the essence of wit.

clue.text: Shabby treatment of natural wood

parts.note: raw means in its natural, unprocessed state
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Unfinished timber treated poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment of natural wood' sounds like varnishing, but 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is unfair handling, as in getting the worst of an arrangement.

clue.text: Measurement of Force Five gale to readjust

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: to readjust is to set in a new order, so the letters of gale and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Adjusting a force five wind on the Beaufort scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force Five' looks like a wind strength, but 'Force' belongs to the definition and 'Five' gives V.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltage measures electromotive force, the electrical pressure in volts.

clue.text: One of Crichton's fans?

parts.note: J. M. Barrie's play The Admirable Crichton, so a fan of the butler is someone who finds him admirable

explanation.surface: A follower of a novelist named Crichton.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Crichton the novelist comes to mind, but the reference is Barrie's play The Admirable Crichton.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is someone who looks up to and esteems another person.

clue.text: What' a bird, the phoenix !

parts.note: the mythical phoenix is traditionally called the bird of Arabia, said to live there alone

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at the legendary firebird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a bird' reads as admiration, but it asks what kind of bird the phoenix is. The stray apostrophe is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is known in literature as the Arabian bird, as in Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Refuge better for a hippopotamus than for Old Bill?

definitions.text: Refuge better for a hippopotamus than for Old Bill?

parts.words: Refuge better for a hippopotamus than for Old Bill?
parts.note: Old Bill is Bairnsfather's First World War soldier in a shell-hole saying 'If you knows of a better 'ole, go to it'

explanation.surface: A shelter that suits a river beast more than a cartoon soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is also British slang for the police, a tempting wrong track; here he is the cartoon Tommy sheltering in a muddy shell crater.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallow of wet earth is a pit where hippos bathe and soldiers took cover.

clue.text: Source of princely income ?

parts.note: payments made to an author or patent holder, which may be princely sums, also name the class that includes princes

explanation.surface: Where a prince gets his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'princely' means generous here: a royalty is a fee paid per copy sold, and the word also means the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty is a percentage payment to a creator, and royalty means kings, queens and princes.

clue.text: They were two for a sovereign after the revolution

definitions.text: They were two for a sovereign after the revolution

parts.words: They were two for a sovereign after the revolution
parts.note: the joint monarchs who shared the English throne after the Glorious Revolution of 1688

explanation.surface: A bargain price, two items for a gold coin, after the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a British gold coin worth a pound, so 'two for a sovereign' reads like a price. In 1689 a husband and wife jointly took the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: After James II fled, his daughter and her Dutch husband reigned together as co-monarchs.

clue.text: Classic egg-laying mammal

parts.note: in Greek myth a mortal woman, seduced by Zeus as a swan, laid eggs from which her children hatched

explanation.surface: A textbook example of an egg-laying mammal such as the platypus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' means from classical myth, not typical: the platypus is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the queen of Sparta bore Helen and the Dioscuri from eggs after Zeus came to her as a swan.

clue.text: In Calais to turn against tho community

indicators.note: to turn is to change round, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going to France and then rejecting society.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial behaviour runs counter to the norms of society and harms others.

clue.text: Record-keeper 'rolled up to work

definitions.meaning: the cardboard cover that holds a vinyl disc
the arm of a shirt, pushed up when getting down to a job

explanation.surface: An archivist turns up ready for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-keeper' suggests an archivist, but it is the cover of a gramophone record; one rolls up one's shirt sleeves before working.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is both the jacket of an LP and the arm part of a garment, rolled up for hard work.

clue.text: Any crest may show lineage

indicators.note: what the letters may show when rearranged is the answer

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms can reveal one's descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry means descent or line of forebears, the same as lineage.
